newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Dillon Read liked Swiss Bank agenda.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Dillon Read liked Swiss Bank agenda.

text.p: The chance for investment bankers at Dillon, Read & Co Inc to have key roles in the SBC Warburg organization led to the decision to sell to SBC Warburg's parent Swiss Bank Corp.

Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, the Dutch financial services giant which pulled out of talks to acquire Dillon Wednesday, did not present as appealing a case, Dillon chairman John Birkelund said in a telephone interview Thursday. ING, which owns 25 percent of Dillon, failed to articulate a clear vision of what a combined company would look like, he said.

Birkelund said Dillon Read, whose managers own 75 percent of the firm, had the option of buying back the 25 percent from ING on June 30 or making a deal to sell out to ING.

"There was no clear definition from our friends at ING about an ongoing operation," Birkelund said. "This lack of clarity, which continued for months and months, made it impossible for us to believe this was going to be a promising combination for our people."
He said Thomas Wyman, one-time chairman of CBS Inc, and a senior adviser at SBC Warburg in New York, set up a meeting with Swiss Bank chief executive Marcel Ospel.
Birkelund said that, at a luncheon in late March, Wyman and Ospel discussed their ideas for how a combined SBC Warburg and Dillon Read would function.

"They presented us with an opportunity so different and compelling that we pursued it," he said. He said although there have been inquiries from other potential buyers, Dillon Read was not soliciting interest and would have been content to buy the 25 percent until the Swiss Bank deal came along.
He emphasized that there was "no personal animosity involved whatsoever" between Dillon Read and the people at the ING Barings investment bank.

As for the future of any link between Dillon Read and ING Barings, Birkelund said, "I think we will continue to work on mandated assignments, as our clients wish us to, that we have already started." But he said that, except for those cases, collaboration will cease and Dillon Read will begin working with SBC Warburg.
He said Dillon Read will buy the ING stake at 1.1 times book value June 30 and when the deal with SBC Warburg closes later in the year ING will receive 25 percent of the premium.

"Everybody in this firm that I've talked with has been so enthusiastic about the opportunities that we don't envisage anybody leaving at a senior level," Birkelund said. He said he expects to play a leadership role.

He noted that Dillon Read president and chief executive Franklin Hobbs will become head of corporate finance worldwide at SBC Warburg Dillon Read, and Dillon Read chief operating officer Francois de Saint Phalle will be deputy head of equity capital markets worldwide and co-head of U.S. equities.
Birkelund also noted there was little overlap because SBC Warburg's existing U.S. activities are focused on derivatives.
